title: A Graph That Looks After Itself: Watching Nodes, Restarting the One That Stalls, and Stopping Safely When That Fails

questions.question: The sensor in a running graph stops producing, and stays active. What stops the arm acting on stale data first?
options: The controller's own watchdog, a deadline of 0.2 s that commands a stop once: it acted at 5.12 s, before the supervisor at 5.17 s
questions.explanation: The fast and local defence cannot be argued with and the supervisor repairs.

questions.question: Why is the supervisor's detection a deadline after the last scan and not after the stall?
options: Nobody knows when a silence begins until the next output fails to come: the last scan was at 4.91 s and it was seen at 5.17 s
questions.explanation: A deadline monitor counts from the last message.

questions.question: The sensor stalls and the viewer fed from it goes quiet too. What should the supervisor do with the viewer?
options: Report it starved and leave it alone with a fresh deadline: restarting the victims leaves the fault where it was
questions.explanation: The viewer was starved 1 time and restarted 0.

questions.question: A restart fails because the device cannot be opened. What happens next?
options: The node gets a fresh deadline and is noticed stalled again 0.26 s later: restart failed, stalled, restart failed, stalled, gave up, 0.69 s after the stall
questions.explanation: After the allowed restarts the next stall is a give up.

questions.question: An optional viewer is given up on. What happens to the graph?
options: It carries on: gave_up() stays false and the arm got 49 move commands in 5 s with no stops
questions.explanation: A give up on an optional node is not the robot's problem.

questions.question: What does a restart give the node, besides the new life cycle?
options: A fresh deadline, so it is not reported again at once: one stall in 6 s gave 1 stalled event and 1 restart
questions.explanation: A node that is never silent is never touched.
